items.prompt: A segment has length 6 cm. It is dilated by a scale factor of 2.5. What is the length of the image segment?

wrong.why: Added the scale factor to the length instead of multiplying.
Divided the length by the scale factor.
Multiplied by the scale factor squared (2.5² = 6.25), which applies to area, not length.

items.explanation: Lengths are multiplied by the scale factor: 6 × 2.5 = 15 cm.

items.prompt: A dilation has center O and scale factor 3. Point P is 4 units from O, and P′ is the image of P. How many units is P′ from O?
items.explanation: The distance from the center is multiplied by the scale factor: 3 × 4 = 12.

items.prompt: A dilation has its center at the origin and scale factor 2. Which equation describes the image of the line y = 2x + 3?

wrong.why: Thought a line is unchanged by any dilation; only a line through the center maps to itself.
Multiplied the slope by the scale factor as well as the intercept.
Divided the y-intercept by the scale factor instead of multiplying.

items.explanation: The line does not pass through the origin, so its image is parallel (same slope 2). The point (0, 3) maps to (0, 6), giving y = 2x + 6.

items.prompt: In △ABC, ∠A measures 52°. The triangle is dilated by a scale factor of 0.5 to form △A′B′C′. What is the measure of ∠A′?

wrong.why: Halved the angle by applying the scale factor to the angle measure.
Doubled the angle, thinking the image gets larger angles.
Used the supplement (180° − 52°) of the angle.

items.explanation: Dilations preserve angle measure, so ∠A′ = ∠A = 52°.

items.prompt: A dilation has center C(1, 2) and scale factor 3. What is the image of the point A(4, 5)?

wrong.why: Dilated about the origin instead of about C(1, 2).
Multiplied the vector from C to A by 3 but forgot to add the center back.
Added the scale factor 3 to each coordinate instead of multiplying.

items.explanation: A − C = (3, 3). Multiply by 3 to get (9, 9), then add the center: (1 + 9, 2 + 9) = (10, 11).

items.prompt: A dilation has center C(2, −1) and scale factor 2.4. Point P is at (5, 3). How far is the image point P′ from C?
items.explanation: CP = √(3² + 4²) = 5. The image is 2.4 × 5 = 12 units from C.

items.prompt: A segment AB is 40 cm long. After a dilation, the image A′B′ is 14 cm long. What is the scale factor? Give a decimal.
items.explanation: Scale factor = image length ÷ original length = 14 ÷ 40 = 0.35.

items.prompt: △ABC has vertices A(1, 1), B(4, 1), C(1, 3). △DEF has vertices D(5, 2), E(11, 2), F(5, 6). Which sequence maps △ABC onto △DEF, showing the triangles are similar?
items.answer: Dilate by a scale factor of 2 about the origin, then translate 3 units right.

wrong.text: Translate 3 units right, then dilate by a scale factor of 2 about the origin.
wrong.why: Applied the steps in the wrong order; the translation gets doubled and A lands at (8, 2) instead of D(5, 2).

wrong.text: Dilate by a scale factor of 1/2 about the origin, then translate 3 units right.
wrong.why: Used the reciprocal scale factor, which shrinks the triangle.

wrong.text: Dilate by a scale factor of 2 about the origin, then translate 3 units up.
wrong.why: Right dilation but the wrong translation direction; A would land at (2, 5).

items.explanation: Dilating by 2 gives (2, 2), (8, 2), (2, 6). Translating 3 units right gives (5, 2), (11, 2), (5, 6) = D, E, F.

items.prompt: A 6 × 9 rectangle is similar to which of these rectangles?

wrong.why: Added 4 to each side instead of using a constant scale factor.
Added 6 to each side instead of multiplying.
Matched only one pair of sides (scale factor 1.5) and ignored that the other pair needs the same factor.

items.explanation: A dilation by 10/6 = 5/3 maps 6 × 9 to 10 × 15 (9 × 5/3 = 15). Rigid motions then finish the match.

items.prompt: Which statement best describes what it means for two figures to be similar?
items.answer: One figure can be mapped onto the other by a sequence of rigid motions and dilations.

wrong.text: One figure can be mapped onto the other by translations alone.
wrong.why: Translations only preserve size, so this describes some congruent figures, not all similar ones.

wrong.text: One figure can be mapped onto the other by reflections and rotations only.
wrong.why: Rigid motions without dilation preserve size, which gives congruence.

wrong.text: The two figures have the same area.
wrong.why: Equal area does not mean the same shape.

items.explanation: Similarity allows dilations, which change size but keep shape, along with rigid motions.

items.prompt: △ABC has sides 6, 8, and 10. △DEF has sides 9, 12, and 15. What scale factor dilates △ABC to a triangle congruent to △DEF, showing the triangles are similar?

wrong.why: Used the reciprocal, which maps DEF to ABC, not ABC to DEF.
Subtracted the sides (9 − 6) instead of finding the ratio.
Compared mismatched sides (15 and 12) instead of corresponding sides.

items.explanation: 9/6 = 12/8 = 15/10 = 1.5. Dilating by 1.5 gives sides 9, 12, 15, so the triangles are similar.

items.prompt: △P has sides 5, 7, and 10. △Q has sides 10, 14, and 18. Which statement is correct?
items.answer: Not similar, because the side ratios are 2, 2, and 1.8, which are not all equal.

wrong.text: Similar, because two pairs of sides have ratio 2.
wrong.why: Stopped after two pairs; all three pairs of corresponding sides must be proportional.

wrong.text: Similar, because both triangles are scalene.
wrong.why: Same type of triangle does not mean proportional sides.

wrong.text: Not similar, because the triangles are different sizes.
wrong.why: Different size is allowed for similar triangles; the issue is the ratios.

items.explanation: 10/5 = 2 and 14/7 = 2 but 18/10 = 1.8. Not all ratios match, so no dilation maps △P to △Q.

items.prompt: △ABC and △DEF have ∠A = ∠D = 40° and ∠B = ∠E = 65°. Which argument uses transformations to show △ABC ∼ △DEF?
items.answer: Dilate △ABC by DE/AB, then use rigid motions to place A′B′ on DE; equal angles force C′ onto F.

wrong.text: Reflect △ABC across line DE; the equal angles make the triangles congruent.
wrong.why: Used only a rigid motion and assumed congruence; the triangles may have different sizes.

wrong.text: Translate A onto D; two equal angles make the triangles congruent.
wrong.why: Treated AA as a congruence criterion and skipped the dilation.

wrong.text: Dilate △ABC by AB/DE, then rotate it onto △DEF.
wrong.why: Used the reciprocal scale factor, so the side AB would not match DE.

items.explanation: A dilation by DE/AB makes A′B′ = DE. Angles are preserved, so rigid motions put A′ on D, B′ on E, and the rays from D and E meet at F.

items.prompt: In △ABC, ∠A = 35° and ∠B = 80°. In △DEF, ∠D = 80° and ∠E = 65°. Are the triangles similar?
items.answer: Yes: △ABC has angles 35°, 80°, 65°, so ∠B = ∠D and ∠C = ∠E, and AA applies.

wrong.text: No: only one given pair of angles (80°) is equal.
wrong.why: Compared only the given angles in order; the third angle of ABC is 65°.

wrong.text: Yes: both triangles have angles that add to 180°.
wrong.why: The angle sum is true for every triangle and does not show similarity.

wrong.text: No: ∠A ≠ ∠D, so the sides cannot be proportional.
wrong.why: Matched angles by letter order instead of finding corresponding angles.

items.explanation: ∠C = 180° − 35° − 80° = 65°. Then ∠B = ∠D = 80° and ∠C = ∠E = 65°, so the triangles are similar by AA.

items.prompt: A dilation has center P(1, 1) and scale factor 2. Segment AB has A(3, 5) and B(5, 9). Which equation gives the line containing A′B′?

wrong.why: Assumed the image is a parallel line with its intercept doubled; this line passes through the center, so it maps to itself.
Shifted the intercept instead of noticing the line passes through the center.
Doubled the slope with the scale factor.

items.explanation: Line AB is y = 2x − 1 and passes through (1, 1), the center. A line through the center maps to itself: A′(5, 9) and B′(9, 17) both satisfy y = 2x − 1.

items.prompt: In △ABC, segment DE is parallel to BC with D on AB and E on AC. AD = 4, DB = 6, and AE = 6. What is EC?

wrong.why: Set up AD/DB = EC/AE, which is not a valid proportion.
Used AD/AB = AE/EC, mixing a part with a whole side.
Added 4 and 6, treating EC like AB.

items.explanation: A line parallel to one side divides the other two sides proportionally: 4/6 = 6/EC, so EC = 36/4 = 9.

items.prompt: In right triangle ABC the right angle is at C. The altitude from C meets hypotenuse AB at D, with AD = 9 and DB = 16. What is the length of leg AC?

wrong.why: Found the altitude CD = √(9 × 16) instead of the leg.
Found the other leg BC.
Found AC² = 9 × 25 but forgot to take the square root.

items.explanation: △ACD ∼ △ABC gives AC² = AD × AB = 9 × 25 = 225, so AC = 15.

items.prompt: A right triangle has legs 5 and 12 and hypotenuse 13. What is the sine of the angle opposite the side of length 5?

wrong.why: Used adjacent over hypotenuse (cosine).
Used opposite over adjacent (tangent).
Inverted the ratio, hypotenuse over opposite.

items.explanation: sin = opposite/hypotenuse = 5/13.

items.prompt: Right triangle A has an acute angle of 38°, a hypotenuse of 10, and a side opposite that angle of 6.16. Right triangle B also has a 38° angle and a hypotenuse of 25. Find the side opposite the 38° angle in triangle B, rounded to the nearest tenth.
items.explanation: The triangles are similar, so opposite/hypotenuse is constant: 6.16/10 = 0.616. Then 25 × 0.616 = 15.4.

items.prompt: A 12-foot ladder leans against a wall and makes a 70° angle with the ground. How high up the wall does it reach, to the nearest tenth of a foot? (Calculator in degree mode.)

wrong.why: Used cosine instead of sine for the side opposite the angle.
Used tangent, 12 × tan 70°.
Had the calculator in radian mode.

items.explanation: Height = 12 × sin 70° ≈ 11.3 ft.

items.prompt: You stand 40 m from the base of a building. The angle of elevation to the top is 32°. Ignoring your eye height, how tall is the building to the nearest tenth of a meter? (Degree mode.)

wrong.why: Divided by tan 32° instead of multiplying.
Used sine instead of tangent.
Used cosine instead of tangent.

items.explanation: tan 32° = height/40, so height = 40 × tan 32° ≈ 25.0 m.

items.prompt: From the top of a lighthouse 45 m above sea level, the angle of depression to a boat is 18°. How far is the boat from the base of the lighthouse, to the nearest tenth of a meter? (Degree mode.)

wrong.why: Multiplied 45 by tan 18° instead of dividing.
Used sine, which gives the line of sight length, not the horizontal distance.
Used 45 ÷ cos 18°.

items.explanation: The angle inside the triangle at the boat is also 18°, so tan 18° = 45/d and d = 45/tan 18° ≈ 138.5 m.

items.prompt: A ramp rises 3 m over a horizontal distance of 12 m. What angle does the ramp make with the ground, to the nearest tenth of a degree? (Degree mode.)

wrong.why: Used sin⁻¹(3/12), treating 12 as the ramp length.
Used tan⁻¹(12/3), the angle with the vertical.
Had the calculator in radian mode.

items.prompt: From a point on level ground the angle of elevation to the top of a pole is 28°. After walking 20 m straight toward the pole the angle of elevation is 41°. How tall is the pole to the nearest tenth of a meter? (Degree mode.)

wrong.why: Added the cotangents instead of subtracting them.
Used 20 × tan 41° as if 20 m were the full distance to the pole.
Used 20 × sin 28°, treating 20 as a hypotenuse.

items.prompt: A kite string 80 m long makes a 52° angle of elevation with level ground and is pulled straight. How high is the kite above the ground, to the nearest tenth of a meter? (Degree mode.)
items.explanation: Height = 80 × sin 52° ≈ 63.0 m.

items.prompt: A 45-45-90 triangle has legs of length 7. What is the length of its hypotenuse?

wrong.why: Divided by 2 instead of multiplying by √2.
Doubled the leg, as in a 30-60-90 triangle.
Used the 30-60-90 ratio with √3.

items.explanation: The hypotenuse is leg × √2 = 7√2.

items.prompt: The hypotenuse of a 45-45-90 triangle is 10. Find the length of each leg. Give an exact answer (or a decimal rounded to the nearest hundredth).
In a 30-60-90 triangle the longer leg is 9√3. What is the length of the hypotenuse?

wrong.why: Doubled the longer leg instead of finding the short leg first.
Gave the short leg.
Multiplied the longer leg's coefficient by 3.

items.explanation: Longer leg = short leg × √3, so the short leg is 9. The hypotenuse is 2 × 9 = 18.

items.prompt: A 30-60-90 triangle has a hypotenuse of 14. What is the length of the longer leg?

wrong.why: Gave the short leg.
Multiplied the hypotenuse by √3.
Used the 45-45-90 ratio.

items.explanation: Short leg = 14/2 = 7. Longer leg = 7√3.

items.prompt: An equilateral triangle has side length 10. What is its area?

wrong.why: Forgot the ½ in ½ × base × height.
Gave the height, not the area.
Used the 45-45-90 ratio for the height.

items.explanation: The altitude makes a 30-60-90 triangle with height 5√3. Area = ½ × 10 × 5√3 = 25√3.
